evidence: voice_webhooks.rs:735-750 — oauth_token_refresh's `else` (has_platform==false) branch mints `voice_access_refreshed_<uuid>`, encrypts it and persists it via update_voice_device_tokens, with NO cfg!(debug_assertions) guard — it runs in release builds too

voice_webhooks.rs:465-498 — the analogous unconfigured branch in oauth_token_exchange IS gated behind `cfg!(debug_assertions)` and returns 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE in release (documented security fix #890: 'release builds must never mint fake voice tokens'); the refresh handler violates the same invariant

Impact: in a release deploy where the platform OAuth client env is missing (has_platform=false), an authenticated owner's refresh silently replaces the device's real stored access token with a non-functional simulated token instead of failing closed
voice_webhooks.rs:436-448 — oauth_token_exchange calls oauth_manager.exchange_code() live against Amazon/Google on every request with no throttle

voice_webhooks.rs:605-618 — oauth_token_refresh gates the same class of upstream call behind voice_refresh_attempt_allowed(auth.user_id) (VOICE_REFRESH_* sliding-window limiter) added by #2769 precisely to stop an authenticated caller amplifying against the upstream OAuth provider; exchange has no equivalent limiter
An authenticated user can loop /oauth/exchange with bogus auth_codes to amplify traffic at Amazon/Google's token endpoint

voice_webhooks.rs:502 — device_id = format!("{}_{}", request.platform, Uuid::new_v4()); create_voice_device (voice_webhooks.rs:522-548) inserts a new row with no ON CONFLICT / dedup on (organization_id, user_id, platform)
Each re-link of the same account leaves the prior device row is_active=TRUE with its previously-issued stored access token still present

authenticate_voice_user (voice_webhooks.rs:1531-1585) selects a device by token hash/decrypt match, so every stale row remains independently authenticatable until its token expires — no revoke-on-relink
